chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from one of his companions, from al-Dahqan, from Durust, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man with a long beard passed by the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). So he (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'What is wrong with this one? If only he had adjusted his beard.' So that reached the man, so he adjusted his beard to be between the two beards (medium length). Then he entered upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). So when he (peace be upon him and his family) saw him, he (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Like this, so keep doing it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended length for a Muslim's beard according to the Prophet (SAWW)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s (SAW) guidance on maintaining a beard of moderate length, balancing natural growth with neatness, a practice deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence as a sign of dignity and distinction from other communities. The narrative illustrates the Sunnah of grooming as an act of following divine example, emphasizing that the beard should be neither excessively long nor shaved completely. This tradition reinforces the concept of 'fitrah' (natural disposition) in Islamic aesthetics and personal hygiene.
